items.title: Integrated Tree-Ring-Radiocarbon High-Resolution Timeframe to Resolve Earlier Second Millennium BCE Mesopotamian Chronology
items.who: S. W. Manning, C. B. Griggs, B. Lorentzen, G. Barjamovic et al.
items.note: Wiggle-matched tree-ring sequences from the Kültepe and Acemhöyük palaces, tied to Old Assyrian eponyms, and found them compatible only with the Middle Chronology.

items.title: Anchoring historical sequences using a new source of astro-chronological tie-points
items.who: M. W. Dee and B. J. S. Pope
items.venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society A 472
items.note: Proposes using Miyake-type radiocarbon spikes in short-lived plant material as exact-year anchors for floating historical chronologies of the ancient Near East.

items.title: Dating by Month-Lengths Revisited
items.venue: Studies on the Ancient Exact Sciences in Honour of Lis Brack-Bernsen (Edition Topoi)
items.note: Re-analyses Old Babylonian and Ur III month-length data and argues they favour the High Chronology over the Middle at high confidence.

items.title: Further Astronomical Fine-tuning of the Old Assyrian and Old Babylonian Chronologies
items.note: Uses Venus visibility and the Old Assyrian intercalation pattern at Kanesh to argue for the Low Middle Chronology, with Ammi-saduqa year 1 in 1638 BC.

items.title: The Origins of the Assyrian King List
items.venue: Journal of Ancient Near Eastern History 6 (1)
items.note: Argues from internal evidence for a fifteenth-century terminus post quem for the King List, bearing on how far its regnal figures can be trusted for absolute dating.

items.title: Radiocarbon offsets and old world chronology as relevant to Mesopotamia, Egypt, Anatolia and Thera (Santorini)
items.who: S. W. Manning, L. Wacker, U. Büntgen et al.
items.note: New annual radiocarbon measurements and the IntCal20 curve refine the Anatolian tree-ring placement and reinforce a Middle Chronology fit for Šamšī-Adad I.

items.title: The IntCal20 Northern Hemisphere Radiocarbon Age Calibration Curve (0–55 cal kBP)
items.note: Revised calibration curve with more annual data in the second millennium BCE, against which the Anatolian wiggle-matches were rerun.

items.title: Studies on the Old Babylonian Kings of Isin and Their Dynasties with an Updated List of Isin Year Names
items.note: Five micro-studies on Isin's kings with an updated year-name list, tightening the relative chronology that any absolute anchor must carry.

items.title: Third Millennium BC Chronology and Clock-Time Correction
items.venue: Cuneiform Digital Library Preprints 22 (published as ISAW Papers 25, 2023)
items.note: Argues that eclipse and month-length data give Akkad and Ur III dates about 50 years above conventional ones, consistent with a High Chronology for Babylon I.

items.title: The Assyrian Distanzangaben in Relation to the Regnal Years Recorded in the Assyrian King List
items.note: Analyses how the 'distance numbers' in Assyrian royal inscriptions were composed and how far they agree with King List regnal years.

items.title: A Synchronized Early Middle Bronze Age Chronology for Egypt, the Levant, and Mesopotamia
items.who: F. Höflmayer and S. W. Manning
items.note: Combines Mesopotamian texts, Egyptian chronology and radiocarbon into a single synchronized Middle Bronze Age framework favouring Middle Chronology variants.

items.title: Establishing an Absolute Chronology of the Middle Bronze Age
items.venue: The Oxford History of the Ancient Near East, vol. II
items.note: Survey of historical, stratigraphic and radiocarbon chronologies for the Middle Bronze Age and how recent radiocarbon work loosens dependence on Egypt.

items.title: A New Old Babylonian Date List with Year Names of Hammurabi
items.note: Publishes a newly identified date list of Hammurabi's year names, adding a source for the internal sequence of the First Dynasty of Babylon.

items.title: New evidence for Middle Bronze Age chronology from the Syro-Anatolian frontier
items.who: V. R. Herrmann, S. W. Manning, K. R. Morgan, S. Soldi and D. Schloen
items.note: Bayesian model of short-lived samples dates a late MB II destruction at Zincirli to c. 1632–1610 BC, linked to Ḫattušili I and fitting High- or Low-Middle Chronology.

items.title: Towards a Radiocarbon-Based Chronology of Urban Northern Mesopotamia in the Early to Mid-Second Millennium BC: Initial Results from Kurd Qaburstan
items.who: L. Webster, A. Smith, M. W. Dee, I. Hajdas and G. Schwartz
items.note: First Bayesian radiocarbon sequence for Old Babylonian-period strata on the Erbil plain, placing the fortified Middle Bronze Age city in the early eighteenth century BC.
